title.narrative: NIHR HPSR-CA - Realising the full potential of the primary health care workforce: Addressing gendered workplace violence

description.narrative:
The consortium aims to fill an urgent and widespread gap to understand the nature of workplace violence and its gendered dimensions experienced by the primary health care workforce in three countries (Burkina Faso, South Africa and Tanzania), where high proportions of women work as health workers and have reported high levels of violence. The objectives are to undertake policy-relevant research to document the nature of primary health care workplace violence and its gendered dimensions, and address the conceptual and intervention gaps in the three countries.
Using desk reviews of policies, ethnographic and participatory action research methods and a survey (in one site), with approaches to engage communities to co-produce and co-design actionable interventions, they hope to iteratively implement and adapt interventions to address the problem in each site. They will invite health workers to be a part of the research team, thoughtfully navigating the sensitivities of researching violence within an active workplace and collecting data with a deep commitment to and practice of ethics. They plan to iteratively interrogate the data to deepen the insights, using emancipatory methods, like body maps and picture codes to get to the tacit and hidden scripts and meanings and co-design, with community engagement, actionable interventions for adaptive learning.
The project take place from March 2025 to February 2023, and will be undertaken by Ifakara Health Institute Tanzania, Institut National de Santé Publique Burkina Faso, United Nations University - International Institute for Global Health Malaysia and University of the Western Cape South Africa and Recherche pour la Santé et le Développement (RESADE) Burkina Faso.
The hope is that this research will generate compelling evidence and extrapolate it out to lessons learnt and actionable case studies on shifts in workforce management to take to other settings. The emphasis is on inclusive and equitable relationships, capacity building, sharing learning and facilitating exchange across the partners in order to seed the foundations of a strong consortium, the impact of which will go beyond geographic boundaries and the time bound nature of the funding.

The project has 4 objectives:
1. To map public health sector human resource policies and assess how they recognise and respond to workplace violence and its gendered dimensions in Burkina Faso, Tanzania and South Africa to better understand the landscape of existing policies. 2. To document the nature of primary health care workplace violence and its gendered dimensions in Burkina Faso, Tanzania and South Africa from the perspective of health workers, managers and community members to reveal the power relations that underline its invisibility and normalisation. 3. To co-design and implement context specific system responses to address primary health care workplace violence and its gendered dimensions in Burkina Faso, Tanzania and South Africa. 4. To assess and reflect on the experiences of these system responses with stakeholders to sustain changes in policies for workplace violence and its gender dimensions in Burkina Faso, Tanzania and South Africa and beyond.
